title: SDK Integration Walkthrough - Polaris Retail
summary: Redwood AE+SE walked Polaris Retail through SDK quickstarts (Python + TypeScript), auth options (API keys, SSO), env setup, and next steps for a pilot. Discussed hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC) for latency and data residency. Agreed to run a 2-week pilot and exchange security docs and pricing.
next_steps: Redwood to send quickstart repo links + example app (Ava)
Customer to share sample traffic profile and SLOs (Maya)
Redwood SE to schedule POC benchmark week and request test dataset (Diego)
Send security pack (SOC2, ISO docs, KMS details) (Ava)

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-06
Time: 14:00 PST
Duration: ~42m
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramirez (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (Polaris Head of Platform), Ethan Cole (Backend), Priya Gupta (DS)

[00:00] Ava Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros?
[00:08] Maya Singh: Hi, Maya here, I run platform at Polaris. we've got Ethan and Priya on the line to cover engineering and data.
[00:15] Ethan Cole: hey all.
[00:16] Priya Gupta: hi.
[00:20] Diego Ramirez: Diego from Redwood, I'm gonna go through the SDK demos with Ava.
[00:25] Ava Chen: Cool, agenda: quick quickstart in Python, then TypeScript patterns, auth and env config, and then ops considerations for Dedicated / Private. We'll leave time for Qs.
[00:35] Maya Singh: sounds good. main goal: we want a low-friction SDK integration so our product team can iterate quickly, but also keep data in our VPC for payments data.
[00:45] Ava Chen: totally understood. We'll show both hosted API flow and what changes for Private / VPC.

--- Python quickstart ---
[01:05] Diego Ramirez: ok starting with Python: simple pip install redwood-sdk, set REDWOOD_API_KEY in env. code snippet: from redwood import Client; client = Client(); resp = client.generate(prompt=\"Summarize order history\");
[01:28] Ethan Cole: can you spell exact env var? we rotate keys frequently.
[01:32] Diego Ramirez: yep it's REDWOOD_API_KEY by default; we support reading from file, KMS-integrated secrets, or the SDK can accept a token at runtime. key rotation is supported server-side, you can create short-lived keys via the Console.
[01:45] Priya Gupta: any retry/backoff defaults?
[01:47] Diego Ramirez: yes, SDK has built-in retry with exponential backoff and idempotency for generate calls; you can override in config.
[02:00] Ava Chen: code quickstart also shows streaming: client.stream_generate(...), which yields tokens. For Python we have example that integrates with our prefix caching SDK to reduce cost for repeat prompts.
[02:14] Maya Singh: prefix caching? is that the KV cache you mentioned in the docs?
[02:17] Diego Ramirez: yeah, it's an automatic prefix/KV cache; if you set up a cache key for common prompts it will hit and reduce per-token compute. works on Hosted and Dedicated, on Private we can deploy the same caching layer inside the VPC.

--- TypeScript walkthrough ---
[03:00] Ava Chen: switching to TypeScript: npm i @redwood/sdk, use REDWOOD_API_KEY env too, example: import { Redwood } from '@redwood/sdk'; const client = new Redwood(); const chat = await client.chat.create({ messages: [...] });
[03:20] Ethan Cole: do we need to compile types for serverless? we run on vercel and lambda edge.
[03:24] Diego Ramirez: The SDK supports both node and edge bundles; for edge you'll want to use the fetch-based client: Redwood.fetchClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }). Also we expose small bundles for browser vs server.
[03:40] Priya Gupta: any CSP or CORS concerns for browser usage?
[03:43] Ava Chen: for browser patterns we recommend routing through your backend to avoid exposing keys; we do have browser token exchange flows with short-lived tokens via SSO.

--- Auth & Security ---
[04:10] Maya Singh: big concern is data residency and key management. we require KMS and audit logs.
[04:15] Diego Ramirez: we support cloud KMS and enterprise HSM for Private deployments. Console has Audit -> per-request logs and RBAC. We can push logs to your SIEM via syslog or S3 export.
[04:30] Ava Chen: also SOC 2 and ISO docs are in the security pack we'll share.
[04:34] Maya Singh: good. how about SSO for team access and role-based keys?
[04:38] Diego Ramirez: SSO SAML/SCIM supported; you can generate team-scoped API keys and manage rotation; we also support ephemeral keys for end-user flows.

--- Env & Setup details ---
[05:05] Ava Chen: practical env setup: 1) create API key in Console, 2) set REDWOOD_API_KEY in CI/CD secrets, 3) install SDK, 4) run sample app. We have a one-file quickstart app that demonstrates both sync and streaming patterns.
[05:20] Diego Ramirez: add to that the config for model selection: you can set default_model in the client or pass per-request model name; we ship curated open models plus our recommended performance profiles.
[05:33] Ethan Cole: are model names stable across versions? we need pinned versions for reproducibility.
[05:36] Ava Chen: yes you can pin model versions in the client and in the Console you can lock a deployment to a model hash.

--- Hosting & Deployment tradeoffs ---
[06:00] Diego Ramirez: tradeoffs: Hosted is fastest to start and has usage-based billing; Dedicated gives predictable latency and capacity for heavy throughput; Private (VPC/on-prem) gives you data residency and full network control. For payments data you'd likely look at Private with customer-managed VPC and KMS.
[06:20] Maya Singh: estimated latency for our region? we are in us-east.
[06:24] Diego Ramirez: typical p95 for small chat in hosted us-east is ~60-120ms token latency for curated models; Dedicated can bring that down depending on GPU selection and batching config. We'll run benchmarks during the POC.

--- SDK advanced features ---
[07:00] Ava Chen: quick note on Optimize: our SDK exposes hooks to integrate Optimize suggestions — batching configs, quantization recommendations. You can optionally enable automatic batching in the client.
[07:12] Priya Gupta: will automatic batching impact tail latency?
[07:15] Diego Ramirez: it's workload aware — you can set a max latency SLO per route; batching will respect that and flush early when needed.

--- Live demo: run sample app ---
[08:00] Diego Ramirez: i'm gonna share the quickstart repo link now - (link shared in chat). Walkthrough: start with python example, set REDWOOD_API_KEY, run python quickstart.py.
[08:18] (sound of typing)
[09:00] Diego Ramirez: you can see the streaming response in the terminal; the SDK yields tokens as they arrive.
[09:12] Ethan Cole: nice, looks straightforward.

--- Questions & clarifications ---
[10:00] Maya Singh: governance: can we restrict model choices for certain teams?
[10:05] Ava Chen: yes, RBAC + per-route model whitelists in Console.
[10:10] Priya Gupta: metrics: can we get token-level cost breakdown per endpoint?
[10:15] Diego Ramirez: Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route and model; you can also export metrics to Datadog.

--- Security / Legal checkpoints ---
[12:00] Ava Chen: for legal/procurement we can provide standard SaaS contracts; for Private we have an enterprise license + support options.
[12:10] Maya Singh: procurement will want termination and data deletion clauses.
[12:14] Ava Chen: noted, we'll include PII handling and deletion process in the security pack.

--- Pilot scope & next steps recap ---
[13:00] Ava Chen: recap: we'll send the quickstart repo and example app, security docs, and a proposed POC benchmark plan. Maya will share traffic profile and success criteria. Diego will set up a POC week and prepare a sample config for private deployment if you want to explore that path.
[13:20] Maya Singh: sounds good. target POC start: next Tuesday?
[13:24] Diego Ramirez: we can start 2026-12-13, yep.
[13:30] Ava Chen: any other questions?
[13:34] Ethan Cole: one thing — pricing for dedicated blocks, can you share ballpark?
[13:38] Ava Chen: yes we'll include ballpark pricing tiers in the email; final depends on commit and GPU selection.
[13:45] Priya Gupta: thanks everyone.
[13:48] Maya Singh: thanks, appreciate the walkthrough.
[13:50] Ava Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up with links and docs.

End of meeting.
